newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks trim losses at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks trim losses at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks recouped nearly half their losses at the end of a thin session's trade Monday and were seen slowly finding their feet, dealers said.

"The market fell today because U.S. long bond yields extended Friday's climb and not because of any political tension, as some would have you believe," said Miguel Daneri at brokers Boston Securities, referring to a new alliance between opposition parties ahead of October midterm elections.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV lost 1.0 percent to 832.72. It had pulled back 1.1 percent Friday on strong U.S. data which rekindled old interest rate and inflation worries.

"A lot of people who held short speculative positions tried to blame the fall on politics, but I don't think that's the problem," one dealer said. "The alliance is a temporary measure to try to defeat (the ruling) Peronists, but we think the Radicals and Frepaso don't have that much in common or stand much of a chance of staying together after the vote."
However, most analysts agreed the alliance could put a medium-term ceiling on prices if opinion polls show the Peronists will lose their congressional majority.
The broad market closed off 1.1 percent, with winners beating losers 46 to five and 14 issues closing flat.
Floor volume dwindled to 17.9 million pesos from an already weak tally of 20.5 million Friday. Over-the-counter turnover slowed to 88.5 million from 96.9 million Friday.

The only blue-chip gainers were petrochemical concern Indupa and cement stock Corcemar, both up 0.8 percent, steelmaker Siderca, which added 0.4 percent, and real estate developer Irsa, up 0.2 percent.
Losers were led by cement firm Juan Minetti, carmaker Ciadea and oil company Astra, which shed 3.6 percent, 3.0 percent and 2.9 percent, respectively.
